tweets.text: The problem with simply buying puts on $UVXY is that you need a very large decline to make serious money. When the $VIX falls, the implied volatility of $UVXY options tends to fall as well, reducing the value of your puts. So you’re fighting two forces: the decline in the underlying helps your position, but the decline in implied volatility hurts it. Unless $UVXY falls sharply enough, you can be right about the direction and still make very little money.

The problem with shorting VIX futures is that you eventually have to roll them, and the longer-dated futures won’t give you the same bang for your buck.

In contrast, instruments like $VXX and $UVXY are structurally designed to lose value over time, particularly when the futures curve is in contango.

You want to bet against the house over time, not just for a day, a week, or a month. These instruments allow you to do exactly that.

David Sacks: Trump Can Save His Second Term by Ending the Iran War

Sacks:

“Your question was, ‘Can Trump fix this?’ I think absolutely.”

Jason:

“What's your top three things he can do to fix it?”

Sacks:

“Just get out of the war. That's my number one, my number two, and my number three.

Because what will happen, the price of Brent crude will drop precipitously.

On the day of the election, the price of Brent crude dropped 10%.

Is that because something changed in the Strait of Hormuz? No. It's because the market started to price in the mere possibility that the war would end sooner, and we got a 10% cut in the price of Brent crude.

It will go from $110 to $70 (per barrel) if this war ends. Gas prices will drop. Diesel will drop. The price of food will drop.

And then the underlying strong economic growth, the GDP growth, and the employment picture, which are still robust, will come into focus. And I think that Trump's popularity will rebound and be back in the 40s.

That's the thing we need to do. And if we don't do that, if the war continues, the Republicans will continue to bleed popularity.”

I like @omarchy! I can be wrong, but I don't see it replacing people's operating system since OS are so tightly coupled with the hardware. I do think it's the next operating system for agents, and soon more agents will use operating system than humans anyway!

The future is ultra-personalized software.

tweets.text:
Wanted to expand on the graduation point from my last Elys post

imo tokens launched on @Enter_Elysium have a shot at the full HL lifecycle:

onchain → HL spot → HL perps

e.g. on RH chain most protocols want to get listed on the RH app as a form of validation. On Elys tho, the next step up is HL itself. huge distro perk for builders

rn most of the launches are happening on @MontraXYZ 

as with every new chain, the first and fiercest battleground is... you guessed it, the launchpads lol

using data from elysa terminal:

> ~65% of launchpad volume in the last hr, ~62% over 24h (vs ~27% all time, so flow is rotating in)
> ~66% of new tokens in the last hr, 11K of 18.6K in the last 24h
> $EACCAT is the biggest trending token at ~$4.4M on Montra,  followed by $BLOB at ~$2.7M on Elyspump and $CHAMELEON at ~$2.2M on Montra
> 3 of the top 5 trending are Montra launches
> ~20 launchpads on the chain rn and Montra is doing ~2/3 of the flow before mainnet goes live Nov 9

will be interesting to see if they can hold the lead going into mainnet, but the flow dominance so far (volume traded, tokens launched, highest mcap coins) is a strong start

anw tech wise, the pad has one uni v4 pool per token, no migration + fee sits in the pool not the token. protocol cut buys back $MONTRA via the kinetiq:native pair, so it depends on volume holding up after TGE (the rev buybacks and xRev narrative here will be one to watch again)

interesting spot to consider from the Elys onchain -> HL spot/perps lifecycle narrative, and imo the tokens with the best narratives will stand the best chance at doing so (i.e. $CASHCAT listing on RH few weeks into chain going live)
tweets.quoted_tweet_text: +the graduation from onchain to HL spot + perps listing is also another distro perk
